IMPLEMENTED. Limb ①: the extractor looks ahead from each FAIL line for the deciding line (Test/Hook/Teardown timed out in Nms | AssertionError | the first `Error:` after it), stops at the next FAIL so no failure borrows its neighbour's reason, and prints it labelled under its FAIL line. Limb ③: each ejection is keyed by the failing test FILE PATH and records that sighting in its own comment as a machine-readable marker; the next ejection reads 24h of those markers back (bounded, newest-first, 5 pages) and at >= 2 DISTINCT PRs files ONE anchor issue per key or refreshes the open one, matched on a stable per-key body marker, then links it from the victim's comment. BOUNDARY HELD: no requeue, no quarantine, no label on anybody's PR, no skip written anywhere — and it is enforced rather than promised, because the harness records-and-throws on ANY unmodelled API and `judge` fails the scenario on that record, so a future call that requeues or labels fails the battery with no scenario having anticipated it.

LIMB ③ EVIDENCE (all four cases the dispatch asked for, all under doubles). POSITIVE (A1): ledger carries KEY@PR#10105, this run is PR#10008 -> exactly 1 issues.create, 0 issues.update; the created body carries the per-key anchor marker and table rows for #10105 and #10008; the victim comment links the new issue number; the comment carries this run's own sighting marker. REFRESH-NOT-DUPLICATE (A2): driven as a PAIR — run 2's world is built from run 1's ACTUAL output (the issue it created plus the comment it posted), never a hand-written marker, because a hand-written one proves each half while leaving the two runs free to disagree about its spelling. Run 2 is PR#10003: 0 creates, 1 update against the SAME issue number, refreshed body lists #10105, #10008 and #10003, and the third victim's comment links the same anchor. NEGATIVE, different keys (A3): this run keys file A while the ledger holds file B already seen on TWO distinct PRs -> 0 creates, 0 updates, and the comment says the key was seen on this PR alone; the deliberately-poisoned ledger is what makes the aggregation prove it only aggregates keys THIS ejection hit (mutation M6 flips it to aggregate every ledger key and A3 goes red). NEGATIVE, same PR twice (A4): ledger holds the same key on PR#10008 under two different run ids -> 0 creates, 0 updates (mutation M5 counts RUNS instead of DISTINCT PRs and A4 goes red). Bonus (A5): a redelivered workflow_run writes nothing at all and does not even read the ledger.

HOW THE LIVE REPO WAS KEPT OUT OF IT. The gate has no network of any kind: `github` is a Proxy over hand-written stubs, `issues.create` / `issues.update` / `issues.createComment` are functions that append to an in-memory call ledger and return fabricated numbers, and every API the harness does not model is recorded out-of-band and thrown so no scenario can absorb it. Nothing in a gate run resolves a hostname. Corpus capture touched the live repo through READS only (get_job_logs, issue/comment reads) plus one local `vitest run` in my own worktree. The complete list of live WRITES I made this task: the branch push, the draft PR #10140, the additive `skip-changeset` label POST, finding #10141, and the report comment. No test run created an issue or commented on any PR.

SURFACE. Beyond the dispatch's declared surface I added two things, both declared here rather than widened silently: `.github/workflows/lint.yml` (the wiring — a gate nobody runs is this repo's own recorded anti-pattern, and dispatch-gates.mjs now discovers the new family from that step) and `scripts/fixtures/merge-queue-triage/` (the corpus + a README stating each file's provenance). No published package source. `skip-changeset` applied additively (POST /labels, never a wholesale PUT) after reading the labeler bot's `documentation`, `ci/cd`, `size/xl`; read back as ["documentation","ci/cd","size/xl","skip-changeset"].

WHERE THIS DISPATCH WAS WRONG, on the record. (1) FALSE: `scripts/pm/ci-failure.mjs` is NOT 'the log-extraction seam limb ① lands in'. The triage bot's log extraction is entirely inline in `.github/workflows/merge-queue-triage.yml`'s github-script block; `ci-failure.mjs` is an unrelated seat-facing CLI whose own header says raw job logs are unreachable from an agent container. Limb ① landed in the workflow and I did not touch `ci-failure.mjs` at all — so #9898 and #9966 are not read-coupled to this card in any direction, and neither blocks nor is blocked. (2) SHARPER THAN THE CARD: 'the excerpts omitted the failure REASON' is only half true, and the half it misses is the mechanism. `AssertionError` was ALREADY a token of the old FAIL matcher, so an assertion DID reach the excerpt — as a detached, unlabelled line — while a timeout produced NOTHING. Measured on the two real captures: BEFORE on the assertion log shows three AssertionError lines, BEFORE on the timeout log shows none. That asymmetry is exactly the trap: a reasonless excerpt reads like the assertion-shaped excerpts a responder has seen before, which is how #10112 got filed. (3) OVERSTATED: the dispatch calls `check-half-states.mjs`, `check-workflow-status-functions.mjs` and `check-cross-repo-closer-outcome.mjs` the bot's 'gates'. None of the three gates it in any behavioural sense — each merely MENTIONS merge-queue-triage in prose (an H12 latency note; a folded-`if:` specimen; a marker-idiom contrast).
